The Puff of Air

English blocks the air, then lets it go with a small explosion of breath. French blocks the air and lets it go politely.

The rule

A plosive is a sound where you close the mouth completely, build pressure, then release. English has six: /p/ /b/ /t/ /d/ /k/ /g/.

/p/  ·  /t/  ·  /k/  →  puff
but only at the start of a STRESSED syllable

Two switches turn the puff off, and both matter more than students expect:

① An /s/ in front: pin has the puff, spin does not. ② An unstressed syllable: the /p/ in capacitor is strong, the /k/ at the front of that same word is weak.

1 · The paper strip

  1. Tear a thin strip of paper, roughly the width of two fingers. Hold it hanging in front of your lips, close, not touching.
  2. Say the French word police. Watch the strip. It does not move.
  3. Say the English word police, with a real release on the /p/. The strip kicks.
  4. Now the second test, the one that surprises people: say pin, then spin. The strip moves on pin and stays still on spin. Same /p/, and the /s/ has switched the puff off.

If the strip does not move on pin, you are speaking English with a French release. If the strip moves on spin, you are over-correcting.

3 · Puff or no puff?

One sound is marked in each word. Decide what happens to it. You will see why after each one.

4 · Say it

Strip back up. Read aloud, slowly, and make the strip move on every bold letter.

Two tired tigers took a taxi to town.
Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.
The control panel tests the power supply, the cable and the terminal.
Now the switch. Strip should stay still on: spin, stop, still, skill, spot, school, star, speaker. The /s/ takes the puff away.

Minimal pairs. Say each cell across, watching the strip. Left moves, right does not.

pin / spin
top / stop
till / still
kill / skill
pot / spot
cool / school
tar / star
peak / speak
Puff itpower · plug · port · test · cable · contact · terminal · PCB
No puff (after s)spin · stop · skill · station · speaker · screw · spanner
No puff (unstressed)capacitor · computer · battery · connection
